bullets.title: META's Muse AI Agent Drives Stock to $700+, Up 10%+; Amazon Blocks Access
bullets.body: META surged over 10% and crossed $700/share after CEO Tobi Lutke announced a Muse/Shop Pay agentic checkout partnership with Shopify, and Muse logged 1.8M downloads and 642k DAU in its first 12 days—outpacing ChatGPT's 1.3M/231k launch pace. Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent from its retail site, with one trader noting this reflects direct competition in agentic commerce. META also announced the 'Petal' subsea cable—first transoceanic cable at petabit capacity—and revenue per employee doubled to $2.9M from $1.4M in early 2023 on flat headcount.

bullets.title: AMD Hits $1T Market Cap ATH; CPU Stocks Rip on Agentic AI Demand Thesis
bullets.body: AMD crossed $1 trillion market cap and hit all-time highs (stock above $600 post-split), rallying ~9% alongside INTC (+14%), ARM (+14%), and MU (+2%). The thesis: agentic AI shifts GPU-to-CPU ratios from 7-8:1 at training to 3-4:1 at inference, with consumer agents like Muse potentially driving ratios further toward CPUs. One analyst flagged NVIDIA's DGX Rubin NVL8 selected Intel Xeon 6 as host CPU as a notable signal; another noted Goldman calculates CPU now outpaces GPU in short-dated capex.

bullets.title: Intel: Evercore Upgrades CIEN to Outperform; INTC CPU Thesis Gains Traction
bullets.body: Evercore upgraded CIEN to Outperform citing AI-driven optical networking demand, projecting 30%+ annual sales growth and $25+ EPS by FY2029 in a market expanding at 24% CAGR to $52B. Separately, INTC surged 14% as analysts highlighted the CPU demand cycle; one researcher noted Meta Muse drives high-frequency CPU task volume and that foundry execution is on track with CPU price hikes expanding upside. NVDA's Vera CPUs also showed 48% better database benchmark performance vs Intel Xeon 6.

bullets.title: META Muse Monetization Analysis: Closing Gap With Google in High-Intent Ads
bullets.body: Detailed research on 654 Muse use cases (12 days post-launch) shows savings, refunds, and personal finance as top use cases; ~20% of users cite cost-reduction as primary purpose. Analysts argue Muse enables Meta to capture purchase-intent signals in travel and financial services where Meta trails Google by 7.5 and 6 percentage points in ad revenue mix, respectively. A2A transactions via Muse Business Agents bring buyer needs, budget, and timing data that Meta historically lacked—potentially a structural ad revenue shift.

bullets.title: NBIS vs CRWV: Nebius Pricing Power Validates Neocloud Thesis
bullets.body: A trader argued NBIS has a more sustainable financing model than CRWV and other neocloud peers, pointing to Nebius raising GPU rental rates by 17-21% despite widespread claims of falling GPU pricing. Oracle also raised pricing for 4+ year equipment commitments, reinforcing the supply/demand dynamic in premium AI compute.

bullets.title: NVIDIA: Open-Source AI Strategy, Vera CPU Edge, and Grok 4.7 Infrastructure
bullets.body: Commentary suggests NVDA's compute advantage, Poolside acquisition, and Hugging Face investment position it as a potential open-source AI leader vs. OpenAI/Anthropic if government backs the play. NVDA Vera CPUs beat Intel Xeon 6 by 48% in database benchmarks with fewer cores. NVDA accelerated computing also underpins SpaceX AI's Grok 4.7 launch; one trader flagged NVDA IV remains negative for the year despite GAI infrastructure IVs bottoming.

bullets.title: CRDO Sells Off Despite 115% YoY Growth; Price Action Analyzed
bullets.body: CRDO posted 115% year-over-year revenue growth but experienced a selloff; analysis points to margin profile and valuation disconnect. Separately, one trader noted CRDO rallied from 167 to 181.2 intraday and mentioned the company alongside semiconductor inspection/testing work. The selloff-despite-growth dynamic is flagged as worth monitoring for entry.

bullets.title: AXTI: S&P SmallCap 600 Inclusion + InP Substrate Geopolitical Angle Drive 12% Gain
bullets.body: AXTI added to S&P SmallCap 600 effective Sept 21, driving passive fund inflows; the stock rose 12.4%. Beyond index mechanics, one analyst argued AXTI may be used as a geopolitical positioning tool in Trump-Xi discussions given US control over InP substrate pricing for AI optical infrastructure. The consensus view: inclusion is a trigger, not the core investment case.

bullets.title: AAOI: 2027 Capacity Target $471M; SIVE Coming Online With 100M+ CW Laser Capacity
bullets.body: AAOI is positioned for a 2027 capacity ramp to $471M per one analyst; SIVE is coming online with 100M CW DFB laser capacity internally plus ~300M total via two external foundries. The analyst noted these supply chains are tied to larger hyperscaler suppliers, framing the setup as a medium-term capacity inflection play.

bullets.title: LITE + GLW to Demo Optical Die-to-Die Interconnect at ECOC 2026
bullets.body: LITE and GLW are collaborating on a high-density optical die-to-die interconnect demonstration at ECOC 2026 in Málaga, using a 1060nm VCSEL platform and multimode fiber targeting CPO/NPO architectures with low latency and power. Separately, TER is explicitly positioning microLED alongside SiPh and CPO for production testing, signaling a shift from device story to manufacturing inflection.

bullets.title: PLTR: Trump Disclosed June 24 Purchase; Stock Up 56% Since; Pentagon $244M Memo
bullets.body: Trump disclosed a Palantir stock purchase on June 24; on August 4, a Pentagon memo directed up to $244M for Palantir. PLTR has risen 56% since the trade date. Palantir's Chad Wahlquist also appeared in a live interview discussing data ownership in AI.

bullets.title: TSLA: Oppenheimer Reiterates Perform; AI Pivot Progressing, Optimus Delays Likely
bullets.body: Oppenheimer reiterated a Perform rating on Tesla, noting AI transformation progress and vertical integration strategy including a semiconductor push, but flagging likely delays for the Optimus humanoid robot program.

bullets.title: AAPL: Tim Cook Legacy Discussion; John Ternus Named Incoming CEO; $12,300 Computer
bullets.body: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman discussed Siri capabilities, Tim Cook's legacy, and named John Ternus as Apple's incoming CEO. Apple also launched a $12,300 computer. The iPhone 18 Pro Max reportedly removes a 20Wh firmware lock upon user activation.

bullets.title: Market Technicals: NDX Volatility Spike, ARKK at YTD High, SPX 0DTE Level to Watch
bullets.body: NDX volatility jumped sharply during the rally with November skew repricing significantly—upside vol now running hotter than downside vol in Nasdaq. ARKK hit a YTD high, trading above its 200-day MA by the widest margin since December. Traders are watching SPX 7475 as a large 20k 0DTE call position that could cause gamma effects; NASDAQ 100 reached +2.5% on the day.

bullets.title: US-China Trade Truce Extension Proposed; Trump-Xi Meeting Imminent
bullets.body: The US proposed extending the China trade truce by six months while China pushed for a longer extension. Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed US-China talks included 'deliverables' on economics and AI, and flagged a potential US-China AI meeting in Shenzhen in two months. Trump-Xi are expected to meet this week with Bessent noting Trump and Xi could meet two more times after.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed's Goolsbee Says Rate-Hike Cycle Complete But Painful; Bessent Eyes Post-Iran Rate Drop
bullets.body: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee signaled the Fed has reached the limits of its rate-hiking cycle, noting further tightening would be 'necessarily painful.' Treasury Secretary Bessent expects rates to come down after the Iran conflict resolves, and repeated that bonds are showing unusual correlation with energy prices.

bullets.title: Diesel Hits Record $6.51/Gal; Russia Extends Export Ban; Oil Slides on Saudi Flows
bullets.body: US diesel prices hit an all-time record above $6.51/gallon (up 76% YoY and ~18% from August average); Russia is extending its diesel export ban beyond September after Ukrainian drone strikes halted the Moscow Gazprom Neft refinery. Brent crude simultaneously fell below $100/bbl (down 2.6%) as Saudi Arabia ramped shipments through Hormuz to 2.9M bpd vs 700k in August. GS Factor Dashboard shows GAI infrastructure factors outperforming while Energy Refiners underperform with negative correlation to AI names.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Exec Warns 'Not Much Time Left to Survive on Memory'; CXMT G5 DRAM in Mass Production
bullets.body: An SK Hynix packaging executive at a US HBM roundtable signaled existential pressure on traditional memory business models: 'there isn't much time left to survive on memory.' Separately, China's CXMT G5 DRAM platform entered mass production with 50% higher die-per-wafer density using SAQP to achieve 11.95nm half-pitch, approaching world-leading specifications.

bullets.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Deal Clears After AG Settlement; $1.5B Film Commitment
bullets.body: A coalition of state AGs settled antitrust concerns with Paramount over the WBD merger; the consent decree requires Warner Bros. Discovery to commit at least $1.5B to domestic film production over five years, a $300M+ incremental US production spend, and minimum annual theatrical releases. Paramount has full regulatory clearance to proceed; the deal had been held up by a ticking fee deadline.

bullets.title: Trump on AI: 'Whoever Wins AI, Wins'; No Liability Shield for Labs; DOJ Oversight Possible
bullets.body: Trump declared 'whoever wins AI, wins' and pledged not to stifle AI growth, characterizing it as potentially bigger than the Industrial Revolution. However, Treasury Secretary Bessent stated the Trump administration will not provide AI companies a liability shield, and Trump separately indicated DOJ may regulate AI 'if we have to.' The administration plans an AI 'czar' to set contours around AI incidents.
